title: In re Aaron Ford, Case Nos. 25-181C & 25-216C (Attorney General)
text:
STATE OF NEVADA
BEFORE THE NEVADA COMMISSION ON ETHICS
In re Aaron Ford, Consolidated Ethics Complaint
Attorney General, Case Nos. 25-181C and 25-216C
State of Nevada, Confidential
Subject. /
REVIEW PANEL DETERMINATION
NRS 281A.730; NAC 281A.440
The Nevada Commission on Ethics (“Commission”) initiated the Ethics Complaint
(“Complaint”) in Case No. 25-181C on September 18 2025, regarding the alleged conduct
of Subject Aaron Ford (“Subject”). On September 29, 2025, the Commission instructed
the Executive Director to investigate alleged violations of NRS 281A.400(1), (2), (7) and
(9). On November 10, 2025, a second Complaint was submitted by a member of the
public in Case No. 25-216C. Upon review, the Commission accepted jurisdiction in Case
No. 25-216C and, after determining that the facts and issues in that case were common
to the facts and issues in Case No. 25-181C, the Commission consolidated the two cases
pursuant to NAC 281A.260.
Subject is a public officer as defined in NRS 281A.160, and the Commission has
jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to NRS 281A.280 because the allegations contained
in the Complaint relate to Subject’s conduct as a public officer and associated implications
under the Ethics Law. Subject provided a partial waiver of the statutory investigatory time
limit of 70 days.
On February 11, 2026, a Review Panel consisting of Scott Scherer, Esq. (Presiding
Officer), Commissioner Lowry and Commissioner Moran considered the following: (1)
Ethics Complaint; (2) Order on Jurisdiction and Investigation; (3) Subject’s Response;
and (4) Executive Director’s Recommendation to the Review Panel with Summary of
Investigatory Findings and Relevant Evidentiary Exhibits.1
Under NAC 281A.430, the Panel unanimously finds and concludes that the facts
establish credible evidence to support a determination that just and sufficient cause exists
for the Commission to render an opinion in these consolidated matters regarding the
alleged violations of NRS 281A.400(1), (2), (7), and (9).
/ / /
1All materials provided to the Review Panel, except the Ethics Complaint and the Order on Jurisdiction and
Investigation, represent portions of the investigatory file and remain confidential pursuant to NRS 281A.750.
Review Panel Determination
Consolidated Case Nos. 25-181C and 25-216C

These consolidated matters are hereby referred to the Commission for further
proceedings.
DATED this 11th day of February, 2026.
